definition.title: Pinned base and component identities are reproducible
definition.setup: Prepare the Friday_rework candidate without starting production consumers.
steps: Record the Hermes commit/tree and the selected Agent Zero, DeepSeek Harness and legacy Friday source pins from the directive.
Resolve the installed build or checkout identities and compare them with the recorded pins.
Record plugin/package versions and dependency lockfile hashes using existing repository tools.
expected: Every running component is attributable to the intended source pin or a documented candidate build derived from it.
A drifted or unresolved identity blocks the gate; a moving branch name is not accepted as a reproducible pin.
definition.applicable_when: Always before the FOUNDATION gate.

definition.title: Friday_rework cannot overwrite the existing Friday installation
definition.setup: Identify the existing Friday repository, configuration, data and service locations; prepare an isolated new home and workspace.
steps: Capture a baseline of relevant old Friday tracked files, configuration hashes and service state.
Start and exercise only the new candidate's configuration/state creation.
Compare the baseline and inspect resolved paths, volumes and service unit names.
expected: Friday_rework has its own configuration, state database, plugin data, logs and job directories.
Old Friday code, configuration and data remain unchanged except an explicitly authorized consumer handoff recorded separately.
No full legacy migration or laptop integration is introduced.
definition.applicable_when: Always; the old Friday baseline is required even when it is currently stopped.

definition.title: All inference consumers resolve to existing local model servers
definition.setup: Use the approved existing server/model inventory and sanitized candidate configuration.
steps: Enumerate Hermes main, auxiliary and delegation routes and all selected A0/Harness inference routes.
Resolve endpoint, model ID, credential source and fallback behavior for each enabled consumer.
Inspect managed-runtime startup/download settings and remove unintended cloud model routes.
expected: Every enabled inference consumer resolves to an existing approved model-server endpoint.
No new model server, model download, cloud inference fallback or developer Astra/Sol production dependency is introduced.
Unneeded optional inference consumers are explicitly disabled.
evidence_required: Resolved route table with secrets omitted
definition.applicable_when: Always; public authorized information retrieval does not count as cloud inference.

definition.title: The main local model completes a real tool round trip
definition.setup: Run the pinned Hermes candidate against the actual selected local main model and a disposable task directory.
steps: Submit a bounded prompt requiring a file read or shell calculation and a final answer based on the tool result.
Capture the model request/response envelope and Hermes tool/result events with sensitive data removed.
Exercise streaming if it is enabled in the intended Telegram path.
expected: The model emits usable tool calls; Hermes returns tool results and produces a grounded final answer.
The configured API prefix, model ID, context budget and streaming mode match the actual server.
A plain-text-only success is not substituted for the tool round trip.
definition.applicable_when: Always for the chosen production main model.

definition.title: The minimal plugin loads through supported Hermes seams
definition.setup: Install only the Friday_rework integration plugin into the new Hermes home.
steps: Run the existing Hermes plugin doctor/list commands and inspect the registered tools, hooks and commands.
Start a clean session and invoke the adapter's bounded status operation.
Review the candidate diff for core monkey-patches, duplicate agent loops and copied capability stacks.
expected: Plugin registration succeeds with the intended names and no built-in command/tool shadowing.
The handler returns the documented JSON contract and uses existing worker/native interfaces.
No new orchestration framework, scheduler, memory stack or browser stack is required.
definition.applicable_when: Always for the selected integration plugin.

definition.title: Single Telegram consumer in the declared candidate scope
definition.setup: Declare staging or production in the candidate identity; select the actual authorized test bot or production bot and inspect its current consumer ownership without exposing its token.
steps: Observe the configured bot identity, candidate gateway and existing consumer ownership.
In the authorized declared scope, exercise one update and verify exactly one receiving consumer.
For a production cutover, follow the existing runbook to stop/reconcile the previous consumer and retain rollback receipts; test-bot evidence alone does not satisfy this production step.
expected: Exactly one authorized consumer owns the selected bot.

A staging PASS is explicitly scoped to staging; it does not claim production cutover. Changing deployment scope or identity changes the candidate hash and invalidates unreviewed carried-over evidence.
If no real Telegram test path is available, this check and dependent USEFUL journeys remain BLOCKED/NOT_RUN; offline work may continue.
evidence_required: Nonsecret bot/environment identity, candidate scope/hash, actual consumer ownership and receipt.
For production: actual old/new consumer transition and rollback references.
definition.applicable_when: Required in every Telegram candidate scope; no missing-credential exclusion. Production handoff additionally requires the actual production-scoped run.

definition.title: Supervision is limited to Friday_rework-owned worker resources
definition.setup: Prepare the selected dedicated warm A0 container and per-job headless Harness launch using existing process/container facilities.
steps: Record the exact container/unit/process ownership boundaries and allowed task directories.
Launch one harmless job for each worker and inspect parent/child ownership and model-server destinations.
Review stop/cleanup selectors against unrelated running resources.
expected: A0 has an unambiguous dedicated Friday_rework-owned container identity.
Each Harness job has a distinct supervised process or container identity.
Stop/cleanup cannot select unrelated services, model servers or old Friday resources.
definition.applicable_when: Always for both mandatory workers.

definition.title: Task directories and gateway-visible artifact paths are established
definition.setup: Create two disposable job directories and the intended gateway/container mount mapping.
steps: Write a distinct fixture from each worker into its own output directory.
Resolve each worker path to the gateway host-visible path.
Attempt an adapter artifact reference outside the assigned task root.
expected: Each job's artifacts remain separate and are readable by the gateway through an explicit mapping.
The adapter refuses an out-of-root reference without moving or exposing the referenced file.
The existing association/artifact contract is used.
definition.applicable_when: Always before worker artifacts can be delivered.

definition.title: Credentials remain out of prompts, artifacts and validation evidence
definition.setup: Use a synthetic canary credential in a disposable configuration field and a normal local test job.
steps: Run the job through Telegram/adapter/worker logging and capture the required evidence.
Search the resulting transcript, artifact manifest, command display and evidence for the synthetic value.
Verify that real credentials are referenced by the approved secret mechanism, not embedded in model prompts or job command lines.
expected: The synthetic credential is absent or appropriately redacted from user-facing and saved evidence surfaces.
Evidence still identifies the route, resource and outcome without exposing tokens.
A discovered leak blocks production use until fixed and rechecked.
definition.applicable_when: Always; use synthetic values rather than exposing real secrets.

definition.title: Telegram expresses the extracted Friday identity
definition.setup: Use the reviewed Friday persona in the new instance's SOUL.md and a new authorized Telegram session.
steps: Send a normal conversation prompt, a concrete engineering request and a question with uncertain information.
Compare tone, brevity, progress updates and uncertainty handling with the approved persona examples.
Open a fresh session to confirm the persistent identity.
expected: Replies use the selected Friday voice and necessary Telegram presentation behavior.
The identity persists across new sessions without copying unrelated legacy instructions or runtime behavior.
Progress is informative and the final answer reflects the actual job outcome.
definition.applicable_when: Always for the intended Telegram experience.

definition.title: Unauthorized messages and callbacks cannot start or stop work
definition.setup: Use authorized and unauthorized test identities/chats and one scoped Friday callback.
steps: Submit equivalent job requests from an authorized DM and an unauthorized DM/group sender.
Attempt a worker stop and an inline callback from an unauthorized identity.
Exercise a normal Hermes clarify/approval callback after the Friday callback registration.
expected: Authorized requests work within the configured scope.
Unauthorized input and callbacks have no worker, artifact or control side effect.
Friday's scoped callbacks do not swallow Hermes clarification, model or approval flows.
definition.applicable_when: Always; include group tests when groups are enabled.

definition.title: Two concurrent conversations retain distinct task routing
definition.setup: Use two authorized chats or topics with different task fixtures.
steps: Start one worker job from each route and interleave status questions.
Complete the jobs in the reverse order of submission.
Inspect progress, results and artifact destinations.

Occupy the configured heavy local-model capacity; issue factual native status and stop through the actual authorized control surface, recording preselected acknowledgement/dispatch budgets and actual timings.
expected: Each progress update, status and result resolves to its own originating authorized chat/topic and job.
No transcript, artifact or cancellation target crosses the two associations.
Concurrency stays within the configured worker/model capacity.
Control dispatch remains independent of a further model answer and preserves admission limits; free-text inference latency is reported separately. Sustained capacity tuning remains DAILY.
evidence_required: Declared capacity, short control budgets and measured native status/stop timings under contention.
definition.applicable_when: Always; use separate DMs if topic mode is not enabled.

definition.title: A real worker artifact reaches Telegram from the gateway host
definition.setup: Produce a small ZIP or Markdown artifact in the selected worker/container output directory.
steps: Publish the completed artifact through the existing manifest/path mapping.
Deliver it using Hermes' supported host-visible attachment path.
Repeat with a deliberately container-only or missing path.
expected: The correct file reaches the originating authorized route and its bytes/hash match the completed artifact.
A missing/container-only path produces an actionable failure or a validated mapping repair.
Delivery failure does not restart the engineering job.
definition.applicable_when: Always for the core coding deliverable path.

definition.title: Harness fixes a real defect, runs the existing tests and returns artifacts
definition.setup: Use a small disposable repository fixture with a reproducible failing test and an existing test command such as pytest.
steps: Submit the task through Telegram and the headless Harness stdin/NDJSON interface.
Allow the worker to diagnose and modify the code within its task workspace.
Run the repository's existing relevant test command and publish the patch/result artifacts.
expected: The original failure is reproduced, the code change addresses it, and the relevant existing test passes.
The result includes the changed files or patch, test command/output and artifact manifest.
No new test/orchestration framework is introduced to satisfy the check.
definition.applicable_when: Always; this is a required end-to-end USEFUL demonstration.

definition.title: Agent Zero diagnoses, repairs and verifies a controlled engineering fault
definition.setup: Seed a reversible fault in a disposable project or owned test service that uses the selected A0 engineering capability.
steps: Submit a diagnose-repair-verify task through the real A0 interface.
Capture the diagnosis and bounded repair in the assigned workspace.
Run the project's actual verification command and collect retained logs and a result artifact.
expected: A0 uses the selected ready capability to diagnose the observed fault and make a scoped repair.
Verification checks the original problem rather than merely reporting that commands ran.
The final artifact ties diagnosis, repair and verification to the same task.
definition.applicable_when: Always for the mandatory A0 engineering path.

definition.title: Malformed or interrupted Harness output cannot become a successful result
definition.setup: Use recorded or synthetic headless NDJSON fixtures plus a disposable nonzero-exit/truncated-output worker run.
steps: Feed a valid completion, a truncated final record, malformed JSON and a nonzero-exit case through the adapter parser.
Include ordinary diagnostic stdout/stderr content resembling success prose.
Observe job status and user-facing summaries.
expected: Valid protocol output is parsed according to the selected Harness contract.
Malformed, incomplete or nonzero-exit cases remain failed, interrupted or unknown as appropriate.
Natural-language success text and transport EOF alone cannot produce success.
definition.applicable_when: Always for the headless Harness adapter.

definition.title: Main, auxiliary and both worker inference routes are observed locally
definition.setup: Enable the intended core auxiliary operations and use the actual production model endpoints in a disposable task.
steps: Run a Hermes tool task, trigger an enabled auxiliary operation such as compression/title generation, then execute one A0 and one Harness job.
Capture sanitized request destinations and served model identities from application/server logs.
Compare every observed inference consumer with the approved route inventory.
expected: All observed main, auxiliary, A0 and Harness inference requests reach approved existing local servers.
An unavailable optional auxiliary capability is explicitly disabled or reported unsupported; it does not choose cloud inference.
Public authorized retrieval may occur but is distinguishable from inference.
definition.applicable_when: Always; disabled optional slots still require an explicit configuration record.

definition.title: Local model failure never activates cloud inference
definition.setup: Use a reversible network denial or controlled stop of the selected local endpoint in an isolated validation window.
steps: Interrupt local inference availability during a main/auxiliary request and each worker route.
Allow the configured bounded error/retry path to run.
Inspect application and deployment network evidence for alternate inference destinations, then restore the endpoint.
expected: Each affected operation fails, waits or retries only according to the configured local-only policy.
No cloud inference endpoint or newly installed model runtime is used.
The user sees a truthful blocked/failed state and recovery does not silently replay ambiguous jobs.
definition.applicable_when: Always before the USEFUL gate; public authorized retrieval is not prohibited by this check.

definition.title: An incompatible model/tool response fails clearly and within budget
definition.setup: Use an isolated stub or recorded response with unsupported tool syntax, invalid tool arguments or an oversized-context rejection.
steps: Trigger the candidate's normal response-handling path with the incompatible response.
Observe parsing, retry and error reporting.
Confirm that a subsequent valid task can still run.
expected: The job reports the concrete compatibility/context failure without inventing tool execution.
Retry behavior is bounded and stays on approved routes.
The failure does not poison later sessions or disable unrelated working tools silently.
definition.applicable_when: Always for the selected local model/API mode.

definition.title: Telegram /stop reaches an active associated worker
definition.setup: Start a long enough active Hermes turn that owns an A0 or Harness job; repeat for both mandatory workers.
steps: Send /stop while the worker is waiting on inference or actively working.
Trace Hermes interruption, the active-agent stop hook and the association lookup.
Verify the native worker/process stop result and retained partial artifacts.
Repeat the stop dispatch while heavy inference capacity is occupied; use the same short fixture and control budget as AC012.
expected: Native Hermes interruption propagates to the correct current worker through verified controls.
The first acknowledgement states cancellation requested until termination is proven.
No successful completion is delivered after a verified stop; partial output remains labeled.
Stop reaches the owned native boundary without waiting for conversational inference; a requested-stop message alone is insufficient.
definition.applicable_when: Always for both mandatory workers.

definition.title: A pending or queued task can be stopped before execution
definition.setup: Hold admission or worker capacity so a task is pending, including the Hermes pending-sentinel case where feasible.
steps: Request stop using the existing stop surface or the verified deterministic task-stop fallback.
Release the held capacity/admission condition.
Inspect worker launches and the task's final state.
expected: The stopped pending task never starts after capacity returns.
The implementation does not rely on agent_loop_stopped firing for a pending sentinel.
If a fallback is needed, it targets the same native control path and is communicated clearly.
definition.applicable_when: Always; use the real selected admission path rather than adding a queue framework.

definition.title: An external job remains stoppable after the initiating turn ends
definition.setup: Start a background job that outlives its initiating Hermes turn, leaving the Telegram conversation idle.
steps: Request stop after there is no active Hermes agent turn.
Exercise the existing stop behavior if it has a verified extension; otherwise use the explicit task-stop fallback.
Confirm the recorded job identity resolves to the intended native worker/process control.
expected: The job can be stopped without a new engineering submission or a fabricated active-agent hook.
No extra customer-facing command is added when the existing supported stop surface covers the case.
When the hook is silent, the deterministic fallback still terminates the correct job.
definition.applicable_when: Always for the supported background-work path.

definition.title: Stop proves descendant termination and reports incomplete kills honestly
definition.setup: Use an owned disposable worker that spawns a child and a SIGTERM-resistant or equivalent stubborn descendant.
steps: Request cancellation through the normal task-stop path.
Observe orderly shutdown, bounded escalation and process/container-scope inspection.
Exercise an intentionally incomplete stop in a controlled fixture.
expected: A completed cancellation has evidence that all owned descendants or the dedicated job scope are gone.
Incomplete termination remains an error/cancellation-pending condition and stays manageable.
Unrelated processes are never selected or signaled.
definition.applicable_when: Always for local/subprocess supervision; use native container-scope evidence for container jobs.

definition.title: Stopping the dedicated A0 job preserves recoverable evidence
definition.setup: Run an A0 task in the dedicated warm Friday_rework container with a retained-log/output directory.
steps: Initiate stop through the existing dedicated A0 environment supervisor immediately.
Preserve job/context metadata, then perform bounded supervisor shutdown if needed.
Collect retained logs/artifacts and inject or observe a late completion response.
expected: The task stops through the native A0 control, with supervisor shutdown scoped only to the dedicated resource.
Available evidence remains retrievable after shutdown.
A late reply cannot overwrite the stopped state or be delivered as new success.
The selected core REST route is not treated as a general history-preserving native pause API; retained evidence is collected after actual stop.
definition.applicable_when: Always for the dedicated warm A0 integration.

definition.title: Duplicate Telegram admission produces one engineering job
definition.setup: Use a bounded recorded update replay or test-bot redelivery with a fixed bot/profile/chat/topic/update identity.
steps: Deliver the same admitted request twice, including repeated callbacks if they can submit work.
Observe the existing correlation/association mapping and native worker launch count.
Complete the original job.
expected: Only one underlying engineering execution is created.
The duplicate resolves to the existing job/status rather than new work.
A legitimate different update is not suppressed merely because its text matches.
definition.applicable_when: Always; Hermes' in-memory update deduplication alone is insufficient.

definition.title: A crash after submit does not trigger blind replay
definition.setup: Introduce a controlled disconnect/crash after a worker may have accepted a request but before its acknowledgement is persisted.
steps: Restart the adapter/gateway and reconcile using the existing protocol's stable job/correlation identity.
If the native worker can identify the accepted job, reattach to it.
If acceptance cannot be proven either way, observe the unknown-outcome path.
expected: A known accepted job is reused exactly once.
An ambiguous outcome is reported unknown/needs reconciliation and is not automatically resubmitted.
Any retry requires the established protocol's proven idempotency or an explicit resolved decision.
evidence_required: Crash timing and native acceptance evidence
definition.applicable_when: Always for both mandatory worker submission paths.

definition.title: Gateway restart reattaches an existing Harness process without recovering fictional stdout
definition.setup: Start a supervised headless Harness job with durable logs/artifacts on a host where the chosen process/scope is intended to outlive the gateway.
steps: Restart only the gateway while the job remains active.
Resolve the same managed process/native scope using checkpoint and association metadata.
Inspect status, durable logs and eventual result without launching a replacement.
expected: The surviving job is reattached by verified identity and is not replayed.
Recovered detached processes are reported without claiming their original pipe/output history is available.
Durable job logs/artifacts provide the result; PID disappearance alone is not success.
definition.applicable_when: Always for the chosen restart behavior; if the host cannot preserve the process, expect truthful interruption and no automatic replay instead.

definition.title: Gateway restart reconciles the same A0 task/context
definition.setup: Start an A0 job in its dedicated warm container and retain its native context/job identity.
steps: Restart the gateway/adapter while leaving the dedicated A0 resource in its intended state.
Read native status using the saved identity and reconcile the association.
Collect the existing result or a truthful interrupted/unknown status.
expected: The adapter reconnects to the original task where the native API supports it.
No fresh A0 task is created merely to recover status.
Unavailable native status is reported as unknown/interrupted according to evidence.
definition.applicable_when: Always for the selected A0 persistence/reconnect contract.

definition.title: Missing or reused process identities cannot cause wrong kills or false success
definition.setup: Use a disposable checkpoint/identity fixture representing a missing process and a PID whose start identity differs.
steps: Run status/reconciliation against both fixtures.
Attempt a task stop through the adapter.
Observe whether any unrelated live process is selected.
expected: Missing/reused identities are reported lost, unknown or already absent only as supported by evidence.
A mismatched PID is never adopted or signaled.
The task is not marked successful and is not automatically relaunched.
definition.applicable_when: Always for a host-PID process path; use equivalent immutable container/job identity checks otherwise.

definition.title: Passing prose or exit zero cannot override failed verification or missing artifacts
definition.setup: Use a disposable job that prints success and exits zero while its required test fails or its declared artifact is missing/corrupt.
steps: Run the job through normal result normalization and artifact collection.
Compare the declared outcome with actual test receipts and artifact hashes/existence.
Inspect the Telegram final summary.
expected: Success requires the agreed verification and valid required artifacts, not prose or exit code alone.
Failed tests, missing files and hash mismatches prevent a successful task result.
The final summary names the actual failure and retains useful partial evidence.
evidence_required: Final normalized status and Telegram summary
definition.applicable_when: Always for all engineering result paths.

definition.title: Session reset cannot misdeliver an old job into a new conversation
definition.setup: Start a background job, then reset or replace the originating conversation with /new.
steps: Allow the old job to complete after the new session exists.
Inspect result association and delivery routing.
Retry delivery once using the same completed job identity.
expected: The result follows the explicit old-task delivery policy and cannot be injected as an answer to the new session's unrelated prompt.
Delivery retry does not rerun the job.
The user can identify which original task produced the artifact.
definition.applicable_when: Always for Telegram sessions supporting background work.

definition.title: Polling and RPC timeouts do not masquerade as job deadlines
definition.setup: Run a healthy job longer than one status/wait/RPC timeout but within its configured whole-job budget.
steps: Issue a short status/wait call that times out.
Continue observing the same job through native status.
Then exercise an actual whole-job deadline separately.
expected: A transport/wait timeout returns partial/pending information without marking the job cancelled or complete.
The same healthy job remains attached and is not duplicated.
The whole-job deadline invokes the actual stop path and waits for termination evidence.
evidence_required: Healthy native status after wait timeout
definition.applicable_when: Always; especially relevant if an SDK/RPC wrapper is used anywhere.

definition.title: Worker outage produces a truthful bounded failure
definition.setup: Make one mandatory worker temporarily unreachable without disrupting the gateway or unrelated services.
steps: Submit a task explicitly requiring that worker.
Observe admission, status and the configured retry limit.
Restore the worker and submit a distinct new task.
expected: The original job reports unavailable/blocked/failed rather than claiming execution.
No silent cloud inference route, alternate unapproved component or duplicate submission is introduced.
The restored worker accepts the distinct task without corrupting the prior outcome.
evidence_required: Original failure and distinct-job success receipts
definition.applicable_when: Always; repeat for A0 and Harness.

definition.title: The candidate stays usable under a configurable realistic job mix
definition.setup: Choose and record a bounded soak duration, expected concurrent chats/jobs and task mix from actual anticipated use; establish resource/latency baselines.
steps: Run the selected mix of Telegram text, short coding, long coding and status/stop actions using existing test/load facilities.
Include at least one gateway restart and one worker failure within the agreed window.
Compare latency, queue/admission behavior and resource trends with the recorded budgets.
expected: The gateway remains responsive and honors configured capacity without unbounded process, memory or retry growth.
All accepted jobs reconcile to evidence-backed outcomes.
The observed duration/load and limitations are stated; no unperformed 24/7 reliability claim is made.
definition.applicable_when: Before DAILY readiness; the duration and load are chosen for the real deployment rather than a fixed overnight delay.

definition.title: Hermes memory persists useful facts without treating cancelled output as truth
definition.setup: Use native Hermes memory with a reversible synthetic preference and a failed/cancelled engineering task.
steps: Store and recall the synthetic preference across a new session and gateway restart.
Run the failed/cancelled task and inspect subsequent recall.
Remove the synthetic test data through existing memory controls.
expected: The intended preference persists through the normal Hermes store.
A cancelled or unverified repair is not recalled as a successfully completed fact.
No duplicate A0/legacy transcript-memory service is needed.
definition.applicable_when: Before DAILY readiness when the baseline Hermes memory feature is enabled; an explicit decision to disable it must be recorded.

definition.title: Native Hermes scheduling produces one authorized result and respects disablement
definition.setup: Create a short-lived test job using native Hermes cron and an authorized test destination.
steps: Let the job become due and record its single execution/delivery.
Restart around a due boundary to inspect reconciliation under the configured policy.
Disable or remove the test schedule and observe the next expected boundary.
expected: The scheduler uses approved local inference routes where inference is needed.
The due job is reconciled without accidental duplicate engineering execution or cross-topic delivery.
Disabled/removed schedules do not keep launching work.
definition.applicable_when: Before DAILY readiness for enabled scheduled behavior; use Hermes cron rather than adding a second scheduler.

definition.title: Rollback restores the previous candidate without damaging persistent state
definition.setup: Prepare the recorded last-known candidate, configuration/state backup and compatibility assumptions from the deployment runbook.
steps: Perform rollback in staging using the documented existing service/package controls.
Open existing sessions, associations and completed artifacts after rollback.
Compare old Friday's baseline and check for incompatible state/config migrations.
expected: The rollback target starts with a coherent state/configuration set.
Job/result associations remain inspectable and uncertain active work is reconciled rather than replayed.
Old Friday remains preserved; incompatible migrations require an explicit backup/restore path.
definition.applicable_when: Before DAILY readiness and before an authorized production update.

definition.title: Work is bounded by actual job and capacity budgets
definition.setup: Record supported whole-job wall-time, concurrency, output/log, retry and model-token/context budgets for the selected components.
steps: Run one task that approaches a budget and a controlled task that exceeds it.
Inspect admission/backpressure, output truncation markers and retry behavior.
Confirm exceeding a job deadline reaches the native stop path.
expected: Supported budgets are enforced at the layer that can actually enforce them.
Unsupported budget knobs are not presented as working guarantees.
Budget exhaustion is reported truthfully and cannot cause endless retries or unbounded fan-out.
definition.applicable_when: Before DAILY readiness; do not invent token controls unsupported by an existing worker.

definition.title: Silence alone does not kill a healthy long-running job
definition.setup: Use a controlled compile/test or local-inference job that produces little output while remaining healthy and within its budget.
steps: Observe the job beyond the normal progress-notification interval.
Request status while it is quiet.
Allow normal completion, then contrast with a genuinely failed/unresponsive fixture.

Using a short existing retention setting, retain a terminal job with pending delivery and a paused/unknown job while cleaning only eligible terminal scratch data; verify user-owned changes are untouched.
expected: Quiet-but-healthy work remains running; missing stdout alone is not classified as a stall.
Status uses available native liveness/budget evidence and acknowledges uncertainty.
A real failure follows the bounded failure/stop path rather than endless reassurance.
Worker resources are released only after execution ownership is settled; pending/paused/unknown evidence survives, while eligible scratch retention is bounded without a new cleanup daemon.
evidence_required: Before/after owned-resource and retained-file observations for the short retention fixture.
definition.applicable_when: Before DAILY readiness for long-running engineering and inference jobs.

definition.title: Operator stop halts repair and prevents automatic revival
definition.setup: Run a controlled diagnose/repair task with the existing recovery/retry mechanism enabled only as planned.
steps: Stop the task during repair and during a queued retry.
Trigger the normal reconciliation/watchdog cycle and restart the gateway once.
Inspect worker launches, repair attempts and retained result status.
expected: An explicit operator stop dominates automatic retry/repair and is not reinterpreted as a crash to fix.
No watchdog, completion notification or restart silently revives stopped work.
A new repair attempt requires the established explicit task lifecycle action.
definition.applicable_when: Before DAILY readiness wherever recovery or repair automation exists.

definition.title: Startup reconciliation touches only recorded owned resources
definition.setup: Prepare owned running, completed, stopped and unknown job records plus one unrelated live service.
steps: Restart the candidate and inspect its reconciliation sweep.
Verify each owned record against native process/container/service evidence.
Observe the unrelated service and confirm completed/stopped jobs are not relaunched.
expected: Reconciliation is scoped to Friday_rework's recorded resources and associations.
Unknown work stays unknown until resolved; completed/stopped work is not replayed.
The unrelated service and old Friday resources remain untouched.
definition.applicable_when: Before DAILY readiness for the selected startup recovery path.

definition.title: An operator can reconstruct a failed task without hidden runtime state
definition.setup: Use one successful task and one stopped/failed task with the configured log and artifact retention.
steps: From saved association IDs alone, locate the source pin, originating route, native worker identity, status history and artifacts.
Repeat after a gateway restart and after in-memory process output expires or is unavailable.
Review the final operational evidence for secrets, ambiguous success claims and missing timestamps.
expected: Durable evidence explains what ran, what stopped, what was verified and where the artifacts are.
Retention limitations and unknown outcomes are visible rather than filled in from memory.
Evidence is sufficiently sanitized for the intended reviewers.
evidence_required: Completed evidence records for both tasks
definition.applicable_when: Before DAILY readiness using the existing logs/artifacts and tiny association record, not a new observability platform.

definition.title: Authorized retrieval/browser work uses available dependencies transparently
definition.setup: Enable only an explicitly selected public/authorized retrieval or browser capability and record any required paid service/dependency.
steps: Retrieve a public or authorized page and produce a source-linked result.
If browser interaction is enabled, perform one reversible interaction in a disposable authorized session.
Remove or deny an optional browser/paid dependency and repeat a core text-coding task.
expected: Retrieval follows the authorized source scope; public internet retrieval is permitted.
No cloud inference is introduced by a retrieval/browser provider or fallback.
Unavailable optional dependencies are reported and do not block the fast text-coding core.
evidence_required: Core text-coding receipt with optional dependency absent
definition.applicable_when: Mandatory autonomous retrieval/browser scope. Existing optional/deferred classification is superseded; unavailable chosen providers are explicit unresolved product dependencies.

definition.title: Vision uses a verified existing local model or reports unsupported
definition.setup: Enable vision only if an existing approved model endpoint supports the required image input.
steps: Submit a small non-sensitive image with a verifiable question.
Inspect the actual inference route and returned result.
Disable or deny the vision route, then run a text-only coding task.
expected: Enabled vision is grounded in the supplied image and uses approved existing local inference.
Missing image support is reported without a cloud fallback or automatic model download.
Text coding remains available when vision is absent.
definition.applicable_when: Only if vision is explicitly enabled and an existing compatible local endpoint is available.

definition.title: Audio capability degrades cleanly without cloud STT/TTS fallback
definition.setup: Enable only the selected existing local transcription/speech path; use a short non-sensitive audio fixture.
steps: Exercise the enabled input/output audio direction through Telegram.
Inspect dependency and inference/service destinations.
Remove the optional audio dependency and submit a text engineering task.
expected: Enabled audio behaves as configured using the approved existing local capability.
Unavailable STT/TTS is reported, with no silent cloud inference or service enrollment.
The text engineering path remains usable.
definition.applicable_when: Only for explicitly enabled audio directions with their dependencies already approved.

definition.title: Optional language-server tooling adds value without becoming a core prerequisite
definition.setup: Use one supported language fixture and the existing selected LSP integration, if enabled.
steps: Obtain a useful diagnostic/navigation result and apply a small code correction using normal project tools.
Disable or remove the language server.
Run the same repository's relevant normal test command and core coding path without LSP.

definition.title: Delivery retry does not rerun completed engineering work

definition.title: Pause and write handoff require observed quiescence
definition.setup: Disposable shared repository with known baseline, actual Harness/A0 adapter and current ownership/stop controls; choose a bounded fixture with observable writes.
steps: Start an owned effectful job, request pause through the existing supported task surface, and observe actual stop/quiescence before any ownership release.
Record file state after confirmed quiescence; restart the gateway and confirm paused intent remains and effects do not resume.
Explicitly authorize continuation within the remaining original budget; exercise DSH → A0 → DSH write ownership transfer with no overlapping writers and refreshed HEAD/diff/read observations.
expected: A metadata flag never counts as paused execution; owned effects cease before handoff.
Restart does not clear pause, cancellation or budget; continuation uses an actual supported session/context path, without promising instruction-pointer resume.
The returning worker observes the repaired filesystem and verifies its new baseline; cancelled work is not revived.
evidence_required: Native quiescence receipts, timed write observations, actual ownership transfer, before/after HEAD/diff, restart state and retained-budget evidence.

definition.title: Uploaded and replied-to input bytes reach the worker
definition.setup: Authorized Telegram test destination and small text/code attachments whose actual bytes determine a repair; include two tasks with the same original filename.
steps: Upload a small .py or .txt fixture with an instruction, then exercise a reply referencing the real uploaded input through Hermes native input handling.

Bind actual input identity and bytes to the correct task; stage into the DSH worktree or use the verified A0 attachment route, and prove worker-visible bytes before dependent effects. Cover each enabled worker transport with the same small fixture as practical.
Repair/check and return the actual output to the original authorized destination; compare received bytes or hashes.
Repeat with colliding original filenames across tasks and an unavailable/rejected input; use existing configured size/type limits and do not add archive extraction or optional media parsing.
expected: Caption/reply selection and authorization bind the intended input to one task; a gateway-only pathname is insufficient.

Missing/unsupported input produces an explicit actionable failure without invented contents or a false successful repair.

definition.title: Owned execution stops when the gateway is absent past deadline
definition.setup: Short disposable DSH and A0 tasks with recorded original deadlines, actual owned boundaries and a preselected existing supervisor deadline or proved stop-on-gateway-exit policy.
steps: Start each worker fixture and persist its actual identity, deadline and independent enforcer.
Remove the owning gateway/adapter while keeping it down beyond the short task deadline; observe from the existing supervisor outside that process.
Confirm effects and relevant owned descendants stop under the chosen policy before gateway recovery, then restore the gateway and reconcile partial results without replay.
expected: A persisted timestamp or absent adapter coroutine is not accepted as enforcement; stop occurs without another user/model turn.
Only the owned task environment is stopped; the shared model server and unrelated work remain available.
Recovered state is truthfully timed out/interrupted with retained partial evidence and unchanged budgets; no blind resubmission.
evidence_required: Actual per-job supervisor policy/identity, deadline timeline, gateway outage interval, independent termination/no-further-effects observations and recovery record.
definition.applicable_when: Required for the core Friday_rework integration using the selected Hermes, Harness and dedicated A0 paths.

definition.title: Warm A0 capacity is released safely for the next task
definition.setup: One dedicated A0 environment, distinct task contexts/workspaces, short observable command fixture and a staged artifact from job A awaiting delivery.
steps: Run job A to normal completion and verify that its owned children cannot make later task effects before releasing capacity.
Admit distinct job B only after actual environment readiness and correct task scope; confirm A cannot write into B or supply B's result.
Repeat the release boundary using the existing controlled-stop fixture for A and reconcile/restart its owned environment when necessary.
Retrieve/deliver A's retained staged artifact without rerunning A, while B remains correctly scoped; inspect the selected native memory/scheduler settings.
expected: An A0 reply alone never releases capacity; late descendants are stopped or have an explicitly accepted continuing owner.
A and B identities/inputs/results remain separate; unneeded global memory/scheduling is disabled or actual supported scope is verified.
Retained output survives worker reuse and stop; pending delivery does not block execution unnecessarily or trigger re-execution.
evidence_required: Native A/B identities, release/readiness and no-late-effect receipts, scoped configuration, retained artifact hash and delivery-only retry evidence.
definition.applicable_when: Required for the core Friday_rework integration using the selected Hermes, Harness and dedicated A0 paths.
